method: 人工编写并在首次推理前固定的合成科技检索诊断集。每个查询只有一个标注相关条目；全文检索使用全部条目，词义排序仅使用同词头候选。仅衡量候选排序，不衡量译文、IPA 或生成解释质量。

documents.title: transformer — neural architecture
documents.text: A neural network architecture using self-attention to model dependencies between tokens. Used in language models and machine translation.

documents.title: transformer — electrical device
documents.text: An electrical device that transfers energy between circuits through electromagnetic induction, raising or lowering AC voltage.

documents.title: token — language model unit
documents.text: A word, word fragment, or punctuation unit produced by a tokenizer. Language models process and generate sequences of these units within a context window.

documents.title: token — access credential
documents.text: A credential issued after authentication, such as an OAuth bearer token or JWT. Sent with HTTP requests to authorize access to protected resources.

documents.title: embedding — vector representation
documents.text: A learned numerical vector representing a word, sentence, document, or other input. Similar meanings are mapped to nearby points for semantic retrieval.

documents.title: embedding — physical placement
documents.text: The act of fixing an object firmly within another material, such as inserting a metal part into resin or placing a specimen in wax.

documents.title: inference — model execution
documents.text: Running a trained machine learning model on new input to compute predictions or generate an output without updating its learned weights.

documents.title: inference — reasoning
documents.text: Drawing a logical conclusion from available premises or evidence. An inference can be deductive, inductive, or abductive.

documents.title: kernel — operating system core
documents.text: The privileged core of an operating system that schedules processes, manages memory, handles system calls, and controls hardware devices.

documents.title: kernel — similarity function
documents.text: A mathematical function measuring similarity between inputs, often equivalent to an inner product in a feature space. Used by support vector machines.

documents.title: memory — computer storage
documents.text: Working storage such as RAM that holds program instructions and data while a computer executes them. Its capacity and allocation affect performance.

documents.title: memory — human recollection
documents.text: The mental ability to retain and recall past experiences, facts, and events. A person's recollection of an earlier event.

documents.title: cache — fast data reuse
documents.text: A storage layer that retains copies of previously computed or fetched data so subsequent requests can reuse them with lower latency.

documents.title: cache — hidden supply
documents.text: A concealed collection of supplies or valuables, such as food buried by an animal or equipment hidden for a later expedition.

documents.title: thread — execution unit
documents.text: A sequence of instructions scheduled independently within a process. Threads can share memory and need synchronization for concurrent access.

documents.title: thread — sewing fibre
documents.text: A thin strand of cotton, silk, or another fibre used with a needle for sewing, embroidery, or repairing fabric.

documents.title: port — network endpoint
documents.text: A numbered logical endpoint used by TCP or UDP to deliver network traffic to the correct application. A server may listen on port 8080.

documents.title: port — harbour
documents.text: A coastal place where ships dock to load or unload passengers and cargo, with facilities for maritime trade.

documents.title: container — isolated application
documents.text: A software package with its runtime dependencies, executed in an isolated process environment. Usually shares the host operating system kernel.

documents.title: container — cargo box
documents.text: A large standardized metal box for transporting goods by ship, rail, or truck, allowing cargo to move between vehicles.

documents.title: race — concurrent timing bug
documents.text: A race condition occurs when program correctness depends on the unpredictable order of concurrent operations accessing shared state.

documents.title: race — speed competition
documents.text: A competition in which participants run, drive, cycle, or swim to reach a finish line before the others.

documents.title: branch — version control line
documents.text: An independent line of development in a version control repository. Developers commit changes on a feature branch and merge it into the main line.

documents.title: branch — tree limb
documents.text: A woody part extending from the trunk of a tree, supporting smaller twigs, leaves, flowers, and fruit.

documents.title: Model quantization
documents.text: Reducing the numerical precision of neural network weights or activations, for example from 16-bit floating point to 4-bit integers, to save memory and accelerate inference.

documents.title: Retrieval augmented generation
documents.text: Retrieving relevant external documents before generating an answer with a language model, so the response can use supporting information beyond the model's weights.

documents.title: Garbage collection
documents.text: Automatically finding memory objects that can no longer be reached by the program and reclaiming their storage, reducing manual allocation management.

documents.title: Latency versus throughput
documents.text: Latency measures how long a request waits for a response. Throughput measures how many requests or data units a system processes per unit of time.

documents.title: Kubernetes orchestration
documents.text: Managing container workloads across a cluster by scheduling pods, replacing failed instances, discovering services, and scaling replicas.

documents.title: TypeScript static types
documents.text: Extending JavaScript with a static type system. The compiler checks types before runtime and removes type annotations when emitting JavaScript.

documents.title: TLS encrypted transport
documents.text: A protocol that encrypts communication between a client and a server and authenticates the server using certificates, commonly used by HTTPS.

documents.title: OAuth delegated authorization
documents.text: Letting an application access a user's protected resources through limited access tokens without sharing the user's account password with that application.

documents.title: WebAssembly execution
documents.text: A portable binary instruction format that runs compiled code in a sandbox, including within web browsers. It can host programs originally written in C, C++, or Rust.

documents.title: Prompt injection
documents.text: Untrusted content attempts to override a language model application's instructions, for example when a retrieved web page tells an assistant to reveal secrets.

documents.title: Vector similarity index
documents.text: Storing embeddings and searching for nearby vectors by cosine similarity or distance, often using approximate nearest neighbour indexes for scalable semantic retrieval.

documents.title: CUDA GPU computing
documents.text: NVIDIA's platform for running general-purpose parallel computation on its GPUs, including kernels used for deep learning operations.

documents.title: Batching model requests
documents.text: Combining multiple inputs into one inference operation to amortize overhead and improve device utilization, with a trade-off between waiting time and throughput.

documents.title: Atomic database transactions
documents.text: Grouping database changes so they either commit together or are rolled back together, preserving consistency when an operation fails.

documents.title: Attention weights
documents.text: Computing how strongly each token should use information from other positions through query, key, and value representations in a neural sequence model.

documents.title: Inverse document frequency
documents.text: A term weighting factor that gives rarer words more importance than words present in many documents, used by lexical retrieval methods such as BM25.

documents.title: limiter.ts
documents.text: async function run(tasks, limit) { let next = 0; async function worker() { while (next < tasks.length) { const task = tasks[next++]; await task(); } } await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: limit }, worker)); }

documents.title: request.ts
documents.text: async function request(url, timeoutMs) { const controller = new AbortController(); const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs); try { return await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); } finally { clearTimeout(timer); } }

documents.title: chunks.ts
documents.text: function chunks(items, size) { const batches = []; for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i += size) batches.push(items.slice(i, i + size)); return batches; }

documents.title: cache.ts
documents.text: function read(cache, key) { const value = cache.get(key); if (value !== undefined) { cache.delete(key); cache.set(key, value); } return value; } function write(cache, key, value, limit) { cache.delete(key); cache.set(key, value); while (cache.size > limit) cache.delete(cache.keys().next().value); }

documents.title: text.ts
documents.text: function escape(text) { return text.replace(/[&<>"]/g, character => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"' })[character]); }

documents.title: events.ts
documents.text: function debounce(callback, delay) { let timer; return (...args) => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => callback(...args), delay); }; }

documents.title: selection.ts
documents.text: let generation = 0; async function showSelection(text) { const id = ++generation; const result = await translate(text); if (id !== generation) return; display(result); }

documents.title: visible.ts
documents.text: const observer = new IntersectionObserver(entries => { for (const entry of entries) if (entry.isIntersecting) queue(entry.target); }, { rootMargin: '300px' }); blocks.forEach(block => observer.observe(block));
